# A tick that a kill stops leaves no lock behind. A tick that its holder still runs is refused. The first tick blocks in git until the file release exists.
[!exec:jq] skip
[!exec:perl] skip
isolate
maintinit
maintfakes
env HOME=$WORK/home
env GIT_BASE=file://$WORK/remotes
env UPKEEP_WEEK=2026-W44
cp blocking-git fake/git
chmod 755 fake/git

# The holder takes the lock and waits in git.
! exec sh home/.upkeep/scripts/tick.sh &holder&
waitfile held

# A second tick while the holder lives is refused.
! exec sh home/.upkeep/scripts/tick.sh
stderr 'another tick runs'

# SIGKILL gives the holder no time to run a trap. The lock must still end with it.
kill -KILL holder

# The git of the dead tick still waits. The next tick takes the lock all the same, because no command of the tick keeps it.
# Its sync fails, which the tick logs, and the tick goes on.
exec sh home/.upkeep/scripts/tick.sh
grep 'sync failed' home/.upkeep/runs.tsv
cp release.txt release
wait holder

-- blocking-git --
#!/bin/sh
# The stand-in for git. The first call writes the file held and waits for the file release. Every later call fails.
work=$(dirname "$0")/..
if [ -f "$work/held" ]; then exit 1; fi
: > "$work/held"
n=0
while [ ! -f "$work/release" ] && [ "$n" -lt 30 ]; do n=$((n + 1)); sleep 1; done > /dev/null 2>&1
exit 1
-- release.txt --
go
